analysis.title: $1.1 Trillion In Cloud Backlog Vs "Peak" Earnings Growth: Two Goldman Veterans Draw Opposite Conclusions From AI's Worst Week
key_insights: Alphabet had the biggest one-day drop in its history on Thursday (Oct 29), Intel fell the most on record on Friday, Amazon reported a disappointing quarter, and the Nasdaq 100 briefly entered correction territory. The S&P 500 still finished October down less than 1%, while the S&P ex-AI index headed for its best month since 2022.

Pasquariello (GS) concludes S&P earnings growth has peaked and the rate of upgrades to forward estimates has slowed versus recent reporting cycles. He is not making big bets now. He still sees the primary bull trend intact, with less upside power and persistent sub-surface volatility.

The S&P 500 moved -0.13% (Jul), +2.62% (Aug), -0.45% (Sep), -0.93% (Oct), while the GS high momentum basket (GSPRHIMO) moved -30.19%, -13.67%, +26.96% and -18.60%. The index travelled roughly 4 points in four months versus roughly 90 for momentum.

Pasquariello says Q3 tech earnings will be remembered as a disappointment: hyperscaler capex intentions are not slowing, but a few large companies missed in the core of their business. Alphabet, the 4th largest index company, had its worst day ever as a public company.

Pasquariello's near-term bull case rests on technicals: sentiment is unequivocally downbeat, the seasonal window has shifted from the weakest stretch (mid-Aug to mid-Oct) to the strongest (mid-Oct to year-end), and the market has cleared a significant amount of length. He acknowledges the bear rebuttal that the same was said into late 2018.

Wilson (GS, London) argues the hyperscaler results answered the AI ROI question 'pretty definitively'. Google Cloud revenue grew 103% y/y with backlog +256% to $561B on roughly $120B ARR. AWS grew 39% with backlog +189% y/y to $578B and management is confident in >40% AWS growth in 2027 and 2028. Azure grew 48%, constrained by supply, with acceleration promised next quarter.

Wilson says the AI financing gap is smaller than feared: Meta completed the first two legs (common and convert) of a record three-part equity raise, Oracle pulled forward its cash-flow breakeven date and says it needs only $20B more to fund capex, and SpaceX added chip financing news.

The article's author counters that backlog is revenue, not cash. Alphabet burned $9.1B of free cash flow (vs $3.5B expected), repurchased no stock in 2026 after $39.8B in the first nine months of 2025, sold $12.4B of stock via its ATM and issued $28.7B of bonds. The GS analyst sees 2027 capex around $350B and 2027 EPS below 2026.

The author cites a running tally of hyperscaler off-balance-sheet obligations that added about $1 trillion in 90 days, to a total of $4.1 trillion. The FT reported Blackstone told Anthropic it may not get an investment-grade rating after its IPO. GS's Privorotsky frames the issue as 'value capture'.

Cross-asset correlations are breaking down. GS AI winners vs AI-at-risk pair (GSPUARTI) rallied 95% from January to its June high and round-tripped to below the start of the year. The Mag7 vs NDX ratio rolled over this week. Apple's three-month realized correlation with the Nasdaq 100 turned negative for the first time since 1981 data begins. The S&P's correlation with its equal-weight version fell to about 0.62, the lowest since at least 2006.

On Thursday Oct 29 about 80% of S&P stocks rose but the index closed down 30bps, an outlier in the sample of S&P down days (GS derivatives, Brian Garrett). S&P ex-AI beat the Nasdaq by more than 3% on the week and the CAC beat US tech by 5%, while France's spread sat at post-2011 wides.

Wilson frames the market as 1997 vs 1999 and cites Vickie Chang's work on macro assets in Fed hiking cycles: about three months of equity indigestion at the start of a hiking cycle does not change the trend. He calls the 2007/2008 analogy for neocloud credit misplaced.

The FOMC held on Wednesday with two hawkish dissents. Dallas Fed's Logan said at least two more 25bps hikes are needed and Musalem said the Fed will need to raise rates 'soon'. Pasquariello says the Fed meeting was largely absent from stock operators' conversation.

The author sides with Pasquariello: hyperscalers posted record backlogs and fell anyway because the backlog comes with negative free cash flow, no buybacks, equity raises and a large off-balance-sheet liability stack. Follow-up catalysts are Tuesday's midterm vote and Apple's earnings later in the week.

market_movers.rationale: Alphabet had its biggest one-day drop on record on Oct 29 despite a $561B cloud backlog, with free cash flow of -$9.1B vs -$3.5B expected, no 2026 buybacks, $12.4B of ATM stock sales and $28.7B of bonds issued.
Intel had its largest one-day decline on record on Friday Oct 30, mentioned without further detail.
Amazon reported a disappointing quarter, though AWS grew 39% with a $578B backlog (+189% y/y) and management is confident in >40% AWS growth in 2027 and 2028.
Apple's three-month realized correlation with the Nasdaq 100 turned negative for the first time since 1981 data begins. Earnings are due later in the week.

sector_views.rationale: Pasquariello sees less upside power and heavy sub-surface volatility, while Wilson sees demand as strong. The article's author sides with the cautious view because of negative free cash flow and equity issuance.
S&P ex-AI hit new highs and is headed for its best month since 2022 as the AI trade unwinds. This is an observation of performance rather than an explicit desk recommendation.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson: cloud backlogs of $561B (Google Cloud) and $578B (AWS) with growth of 103%, 39% and 48%, no sign of demand slowing, and a financing gap smaller than feared (Meta equity raise, Oracle needing only $20B more).
tension_points.bear_case: The article and Pasquariello: backlog is revenue not cash. Alphabet burned $9.1B of free cash flow, stopped buybacks and sold equity and bonds. Earnings growth has peaked and estimate upgrades are slowing. Off-balance-sheet obligations reached $4.1 trillion.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Wilson expects clearing the midterms to unlock a year-end rally. The bull view is also tested by Apple's earnings later in the week and by Azure accelerating next quarter as promised.

tension_points.bull_case: Pasquariello: the primary bull trend is intact, sentiment is unequivocally downbeat, seasonality turns favourable from mid-October, and length has been cleared. Wilson: equity indigestion of about three months at the start of a hiking cycle does not change the trend.
tension_points.bear_case: The bears could argue the same was said into late 2018. The bull case rests on a Fed hiking cycle, with two hawkish dissents and calls for at least two more 25bps hikes.
